Behaviour of init_section_page_ext, page_to_pfn, pfn_to_page, pfn_to_nid, pfn_to_online_page, and SECTION_ALIGN helpers.

Reference counting, compound order, frozen page release, and head page resolution semantics for fragment pages.
Layout of struct folio, struct page, and folio helpers for LRU, idle, young, lock, mapping, and reference management.
Layout of struct page_vma_mapped_walk, struct vm_area_struct, reverse mapping walk control, and PVMW flag values.
Page table traversal helpers, huge page handling, migration and device entry encoding, and table lock acquisition rules.

Maximum frame number, idle bitmap persistence, and interaction of idle marking with reclaim beyond what is shown.

findings.text: The extension table offers lookup helpers that resolve a frame number or page descriptor to its side record, plus paired acquire and release helpers and a physical address variant that first requires the frame to be online.

A side table pointer is treated as absent when null or when its marker bits are set; lookup returns no entry in that case instead of indexing, which covers boot and hotplug windows where the per section array is not yet present.

Reads of the per section side pointer use single access atomic helpers under a read side critical section; lookup warns when that protection is missing, acquire holds it across use, and release drops it while tolerating a null handle.

Bringing a range online expands it to whole sections, initializes each section table in order, and on first failure walks back over the already initialized prefix freeing it before reporting out of memory; success leaves all sections initialized.

Taking a range offline expands it to whole sections then proceeds in three passes: mark every section pointer invalid, wait for preexisting readers to drain, then clear and release each table, preventing access to freed storage.

A memory hotplug notifier dispatches lifecycle events to the side table manager: going online builds tables with error propagation, going offline requests are ignored, completed offline and cancelled online both tear tables down, and completed online and cancelled offline do nothing.

Releasing a section table adjusts the map census by its size, then follows one of two paths based on address kind: one path returns virtual allocation storage, the other validates the backing page is not reserved, detaches leak tracking, and releases the exact byte extent.

Section teardown is idempotent for missing state; when the stored pointer carries the invalid marker it is first normalized back before clearing the slot and freeing the entry that corresponds to the section start.

The fragment cache exposes drain, low level drain, aligned allocation, and single fragment release operations that work on a caller owned cache object holding a packed page handle, a bias count, and a current offset.

The cache handle packs three fields into one word: the page address aligned to page size, a small allocation order in the low bits, and a single flag recording whether the page came from the emergency reserve; helpers extract each field and derive the page descriptor from the address portion.

Refill prefers a large backing page with reclaim restricted and failure tolerant allocation attributes when the platform page is smaller than the cache maximum, otherwise falls back to a single page; failure stores an empty handle and allocation reports no memory.

Aligned allocation refills when empty, then aligns the cached offset and either carves the fragment while updating bias and offset or recycles the current page when space is exhausted by dropping the bias, replacing reserve backed pages, or resetting counts when exclusive, before retrying with a fresh page if sharing persists.

Drain paths subtract a caller supplied or cached bias from the page reference count and only return the page to the allocator when the count reaches zero, using the compound order for the release; an empty cache handle makes drain a no operation and clears the handle after use.

A request larger than one platform page that does not fit the current cache fails without discarding the cached page, avoiding additional pressure under low memory; successful reuse never uses atomic reset while the page may still be observed by other get paths.
Idle tracking transfers state in units of one 64 bit word, with chunk bit capacity defined as byte size times bits per byte; file positions and transfer lengths must be multiples of that unit.

Idle operations only consider frames that resolve to an online head page whose folio is on the reclaim list and can be referenced; the folio identity and reclaim membership are rechecked after acquiring the reference and rejected if changed.

Clearing references skips folios that are unmapped or lack raw mapping state, then attempts a nonblocking folio lock and walks reverse mappings under a shared anon lock before unlocking; the walk control is reused as unchanging.

The per mapping scan clears architecture young indicators at leaf and huge levels and consults device notifiers; if any mapping showed youth the folio is marked not idle and marked young so later reclaim sampling observes activity, with subpage activity promoting the entire huge folio.

Reading the idle bitmap converts file position and length from bytes to frames, clamps to the maximum frame, and for each frame reports set only when its folio exists and remains idle after clearing hardware references; positions beyond the limit return empty and misaligned access is rejected.

Writing the bitmap uses the same position conversion and clamping, and for each set input bit clears hardware references then marks the corresponding folio idle when present; positions beyond the limit are rejected as out of range and misaligned access is rejected.

Idle tracking is exposed as a binary sysfs group named page_idle containing a single bitmap object with mode 0600 for owner read write; initialization creates that group under the memory object and reports failures to the log.

The reverse mapping walk offers an iterator that advances a cursor over one address space range and reports each mapping of a target frame span, plus a completion helper that releases locks and mapping state when no further match exists.

Iteration descends the table hierarchy skipping absent levels by aligning forward, handles huge and transparent huge entries at the middle level, otherwise maps the leaf table and scans forward across entries and table boundaries until a matching entry is found or the range end is reached.

Ranges backed by huge translation use a dedicated walk that allows at most one mapping attempt per cursor, requires the caller to already hold the file mapping lock, and validates the entry against the huge page span before reporting success.

Whether migration entries and device private or exclusive entries are accepted depends on a caller supplied migration flag: normal scans accept present and device entries but reject migration, while migration scans do the opposite, and transparent huge present checks reject migration mode.

The walk holds the appropriate table lock for the level being examined, using the huge lock for huge entries, the middle level lock for huge checks, and the leaf lock for leaf scans, releasing before crossing tables and revalidating the middle entry after acquiring the leaf lock to detect concurrent splits.

Match testing extracts the entry frame number through present or swap decoding as appropriate and reports success only when the entry span overlaps the target span, using single page span for leaves and huge span for middle entries.

The walk tolerates concurrent table changes by resampling middle entries without locking, restarting when the sampled value changed under it, treating a split huge entry as leaf level work, and recording boundary crossings; a strict synchronization mode uses locked leaf mapping and may synchronize middle entries before skipping.

Side table lookup must handle calls from allocator sanity checks before tables exist by returning absent, and fragment release asserts the backing page still holds at least one reference before dropping counts.
Forward skipping rounds the cursor up to the skipped level size and saturates a wrap to zero into the maximum address so iteration terminates instead of cycling.
